## Candidate finding HL-1 — this affects how the H-LIFE results will read

In plain terms: **a removed `<splat-site>` never gets freed from memory.**
- **Measured without my test page:** in a bare page, one element was loaded, removed and every reference dropped. After forced memory clean-ups, the element, its runtime, renderer and splat mesh were still alive. Five throwaway control objects in the same page were freed within about 10 seconds. Same result on WebGL2 and WebGPU.
- **Cost:** on WebGL2 each retained runtime keeps its large texture arrays, so memory grew about 1 GB per cycle at first. On WebGPU the heavy data is on the GPU and is freed (counters return exactly to zero), so memory readings stay flat and WebGPU's gates pass.
- **Unknown:** what holds it. I've ruled out the element's and runtime's global listeners, globals, and console logging. I can't rule out three.js internals, other parts of the runtime, or the debugging connection both browsers run under. A heap snapshot would name the holder; my tools can't take one.
